review.note: A9: the item's own P625 is (2, 28) at one degree — Algeria's centroid, not a place — so it was refused rather than written as a place named after a massacre; P276 is empty and P131 names Kherrata, one of the three towns. A7: the item ends it on 12 May 1945 and the cached lead at revision 1373304371 says "in May and June 1945", so the end is June. No start day is stated and none was supplied. Filed by the item's own P361 chain, which climbs through "Algeria in World War II" to Q362.

title: Sétif and Guelma massacre
summary: The English Wikipedia article "Sétif and Guelma massacre", at revision 1373304371, opens: "The Sétif and Guelma massacre was a series of massacres by French colonial authorities and pied-noir European settler militias on Algerian civilians in May and June 1945 around the towns of Sétif and Guelma in French Algeria." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Wikidata item Q593024, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "massacre in Algeria in 1945". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
